record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Analyze the strong iISS concept in infinite-dimensional systems, extending the finite-dimensional ODE notion and the brief discussion given in this survey. The goal is to determine its properties, scope, and role in infinite-dimensional stability theory.

evidence.quote: • Strong iISS concept, introduced in [32] for ODEs and briefly discussed in this survey (Sections 2.5, 3.6), has not been analyzed till now.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Consider an infinite-dimensional control system

  ẋ(t) = F(x(t), u(t)),  x(t) ∈ X,  u ∈ U_c,

where X is a Banach state space, U_c is a space of admissible input functions u : [0,∞) → U taking values in a normed input space U (for instance L^∞_loc([0,∞); U)), and F generates a well-posed semiflow φ(t, x, u) with φ(0, x, u) = x. Denote by K the class of continuous, strictly increasing functions α : [0,∞) → [0,∞) with α(0) = 0; by K_∞ the subclass of unbounded such functions; and by KL the class of continuous β : [0,∞)² → [0,∞) such that β(·, t) ∈ K for each t and β(r, t) ↓ 0 as t → ∞.

Recall:
• The system is input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K such that for every x ∈ X and admissible u,
  ‖φ(t, x, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_∞)  for all t ≥ 0.
• The system is integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and α, γ ∈ K_∞ such that
  α(‖φ(t, x, u)‖_X) ≤ β(‖x‖_X, t) + ∫_0^t γ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds  for all t ≥ 0.
• Following the finite-dimensional definition, call the system strongly iISS if it is iISS and additionally ISS with respect to small inputs, i.e. there exist β ∈ KL, γ ∈ K, and a constant R > 0 such that for all admissible u with ‖u‖_∞ ≤ R,
  ‖φ(t, x, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_∞)  for all t ≥ 0, x ∈ X.

Problem. Develop a theory of strong iISS for such infinite-dimensional control systems. In particular:
(a) Establish equivalent Lyapunov-function characterizations of strong iISS (e.g. the existence of a smooth iISS-Lyapunov function whose dissipation rate is positive definite, together with a small-input ISS condition).
(b) Determine the precise relationship of strong iISS to ISS, iISS, and to the existence of asymptotic gains, including whether strong iISS is strictly stronger than iISS and strictly weaker than ISS in the infinite-dimensional setting.
(c) Prove or disprove that strong iISS is preserved under cascade interconnection of infinite-dimensional systems and analyze its behaviour under feedback and small-gain interconnections.
(d) Identify nontrivial classes of infinite-dimensional systems (e.g. linear systems with unbounded admissible input operators, semilinear evolution equations, bilinear control systems on Hilbert spaces) for which strong iISS can be verified, and provide checkable sufficient conditions in these classes.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent research has begun to develop strong iISS / strong ISS notions in infinite dimensions. Works on characterizations of ISS and iISS for infinite-dimensional and non-autonomous systems (e.g. Mironchenko-Wirth and follow-ups, and the 2022 characterization of integral ISS for time-varying systems of infinite dimension) have produced partial results, including Lyapunov-type characterizations and preservation under cascades, but a full systematic theory matching the finite-dimensional strong iISS framework does not yet appear complete in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems: Recent Results and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists strong iISS in infinite dimensions as not yet analyzed.
status_evidence.claim: The survey explicitly states that strong iISS in infinite dimensions has not been analyzed.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of integral input-to-state stability for nonlinear time-varying systems of infinite dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Provides characterizations of iISS for infinite-dimensional time-varying systems.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on iISS characterizations in infinite dimensions has appeared after 2019.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-state stability of non-autonomous infinite-dimensional control systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies ISS and iISS of non-autonomous infinite-dimensional systems with indefinite Lyapunov functions.
status_evidence.claim: Related ISS/iISS frameworks have been developed but not a complete strong-iISS theory.
